Core command policy is bypassed: When command policy is omitted, the resolver creates an allow gate; later command detection treats control text as explicit when CommandAuthorized is true.
Sibling channels preserve resolver-derived command authority: Buzz and Nextcloud Talk compute command policy and pass access.commandAccess.authorized into the inbound context instead of forcing authorization. | | **Findings** | 2 actionable findings | [P1] Preserve command authorization for A2A text turns
[P1] Scope outbound A2A context to the local conversation | | **Security** | Needs attention | Authenticated peer bypasses command authorization: The adapter marks every admitted A2A peer command-authorized without using the core command-policy decision, allowing a peer token to reach textual control commands that the normal command allowlists would deny. | ## How this fits together The A2A plugin converts authenticated HTTP/JSON-RPC peer traffic into OpenClaw channel ingress, then returns agent output as A2A task artifacts. Outbound channel messages become A2A requests to configured peers, so ingress authorization and remote conversation context affect agent safety and state isolation. ```mermaid flowchart LR Peer[A2A peer] --> Http[HTTP JSON-RPC routes] Http --> Auth[Peer token check] Auth --> Ingress[Channel ingress policy] Ingress --> Agent[OpenClaw agent session] Agent --> Outbound[Outbound A2A delivery] Outbound --> Context[Remote peer conversation context] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should A2A ship as a bundled official plugin, or should this optional interoperability capability be published as an external official plugin? | **Publish externally:** Move the A2A package to an external official plugin while retaining only generic plugin seams in core. | Why: The implementation uses existing plugin seams and adds a new default-off bundled capability, so distribution scope requires maintainer intent beyond the two concrete repair findings. ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve command authorization for A2A text turns (P1)** - This sets `CommandAuthorized` for every authenticated peer after resolving ingress without a command policy. Consequently, a configured peer can send a slash/control command and bypass command-owner and access-group authorization. Compute command applicability through the channel runtime, pass it to the resolver, reject `shouldBlockControlCommand`, and carry `ingress.commandAccess.authorized` into the context. - [ ] **Scope outbound A2A context to the local conversation (P1)** - All sends to a peer use the same `ctx-oc-<peer>` context ID. The local outbound route is agent-specific, so messages from distinct local agents to one remote peer are merged into one remote A2A conversation and can expose or contaminate state. Carry an originating conversation identity to delivery and derive a stable context from it; update the peer-context test accordingly. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Authenticated peer bypasses command authorization** - The adapter marks every admitted A2A peer command-authorized without using the core command-policy decision, allowing a peer token to reach textual control commands that the normal command allowlists would deny. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Bundling this optional interoperability channel rather than distributing it as an external official plugin remains a maintainer product decision under the repository’s lean-core direction. ## Findings - [P1] Preserve command authorization for A2A text turns — `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts:93` - [P1] Scope outbound A2A context to the local conversation — `extensions/a2a/src/outbound.ts:67` - [high] Authenticated peer bypasses command authorization — `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts:93`
